issue.title: Fine-grained: Support Python 3 unpacking expressions (and fix crash)
issue.body:
Also fix crash on incompatible dictionary unpack. Fixes #4959.

Work towards #4951.

body: Based on `first, *other = [None, *a]` working correctly I'm guessing with `first, *other = [*a, None]` we are trying to unpack `*a` into `first`, and `None` into `*other`, which is wrong.

body: (Bumping priority to high since this appeared again in the context of mypyc)

I think the cop-out way to fix this would be to have `check_assignment_to_multiple_lvalues` not recurse into a ListExpr/TupleExpr if the rhs has a star expression, or maybe as more of a compromise, check the lvalues *up to* the right-hand-side's star individually, then check the rest via `check_multi_assignment`.

issue.title: Unpacking starred expressions in tuples
issue.body:
(migrated from [a comment](https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/1178#issuecomment-545327224) in #1178 at @ethanhs's request)

There seems to an issue with unpacking things when they are part of a tuple on the right side of assignment. #1178 is related, but specifically deals with variable-length tuples (and using `len()` to distinguish them). The current issue occurs even for fixed-length and type-annotated tuples.

```python
# file: ex.py
from typing import Tuple
points = (1, 2)  # type: Tuple[int, int]
x, y, z = *points, 0
```

This results in incorrect inference about the tuple size (but Python does not complain, only mypy):

```console
$ mypy ex.py 
ex.py:4: error: Need more than 2 values to unpack (3 expected)
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 1 source file)
```

A workaround is to use cast(), as @JukkaL [suggested](https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/1178#issuecomment-176185607):

```python
x, y, z = cast(Tuple[int, int, int], (*points, 0))
```

And here's my versions of Python and mypy:

```console
$ mypy --version
mypy 0.740
$ python --version
Python 3.7.3
```

body:
I came across this error when working on #7779. I think both issues will be fixed by the same solution.

@refi64 I don't think getting the index of the starred expression will work the same as it does for lvalues, because the star does really different things on an lvalue vs an rvalue, and there can be more than one:

```python
a = (1, 2, 3)
first, *other = *a, 4        # mypy: crash
print(other)                 # python: [2, 3, 4]
first, *other = *(*a, 4), 5  # mypy: crash
print(other)                 # python: [2, 3, 4, 5]
first, *other = *a, *a       # mypy: crash
print(other)                 # python: [2, 3, 1, 2, 3]
```

Another similar looking example reported in #8635:

```py
a, b = *(1, 2)
```

```python3
a, b = *tup
```
Looks like flake8 does not pick up on this being a syntax error.

issue.title: Fix crashes with unpacking SyntaxError
issue.body:
In general, mypy doesn't promise to be able to check the remainder of
your code in the presence of syntax errors, so just make this a blocking
error.

Fixes #9137
Fixes #3825 (most of the reports in this issue were fixed by #8827)

body:

We'll use https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/9137 to track remaining issue, including thejcannon's example
